question: Which body fluid is excluded from Standard Precautions unless it contains visible blood?
explanation: Sweat does not transmit bloodborne pathogens and is excluded from Standard Precautions unless visible blood is present. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h1)

question: Why did Universal Precautions eventually expand into the broader term Standard Precautions?

options.A: To replace handwashing requirements with alcohol rubs entirely
options.B: To cover all body fluids and moist tissues, not just blood
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing protective gloves
options.D: To focus exclusively on airborne infections in rural clinics

explanation: Standard Precautions expanded the original blood-only focus to include all body fluids, secretions, and excretions except sweat. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h1)

question: What is the primary assumption underlying Universal Precautions in clinical practice?

options.A: Visible dirt indicates the presence of bloodborne viruses
options.B: Only patients with chronic illnesses require isolation
options.C: Every patient is treated as potentially infectious
options.D: Healthy individuals cannot transmit hospital pathogens

explanation: Universal Precautions rely on treating all patients as potentially infectious to prevent accidental exposure. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h2)

question: A nurse in a busy clinic skips wearing gloves for a patient who looks healthy. Which safety principle is being ignored?

options.A: Treating every patient as potentially infectious
options.B: Applying surgical asepsis to sterile body cavities
options.C: Ensuring proper ventilation in isolation rooms
options.D: Reducing biomedical waste generation at the source

explanation: Asymptomatic patients can still carry bloodborne pathogens, making universal barrier use mandatory for everyone. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h2)

question: What is the correct action regarding disposable examination gloves after patient care?

options.A: Discard them immediately in the appropriate waste bin
options.B: Immerse them in a chlorine solution and hang to dry
options.C: Wash them with soap and water for the next patient
options.D: Wipe them with alcohol rub and store in your pocket

explanation: Disposable gloves are single-use items that must be discarded immediately after use to prevent cross-contamination. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h3)

question: In what order should a nurse remove full personal protective equipment after a procedure?

options.A: Mask first, followed by gown, gloves, and eye protection
options.B: Gown first, followed by gloves, mask, and eye protection
options.C: Eye protection first, followed by mask, gown, and gloves
options.D: Gloves first, followed by eye protection, gown, and mask

explanation: Removing gloves first prevents contaminating other equipment or the skin during the doffing process. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h3)

question: When must a nurse choose handwashing with soap and water over alcohol-based hand rub?

options.A: When hands are visibly soiled with blood or body fluids
options.B: Immediately before taking a patient's temperature
options.C: After touching the clean bedside table in a ward
options.D: When moving between two stable patients in beds

explanation: Soap and water are required to physically remove visible organic matter and bacterial spores from soiled hands. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h4)

question: According to the WHO Five Moments, when should a nurse perform hand hygiene after touching a patient?

options.A: Immediately after leaving the patient's bedside
options.B: At the end of the entire nursing shift on the ward
options.C: Only if the nurse touched an open surgical wound
options.D: Before touching the patient's immediate environment

explanation: Hand hygiene is required after patient contact to remove any transient microorganisms picked up during care. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h4)

question: Why must healthcare workers NEVER recap used needles with two hands?

options.A: It wastes valuable time during emergency medication administration
options.B: It causes the plastic syringe barrel to crack under pressure
options.C: It ruins the sharpness of the needle bevel for future use
options.D: It is the leading cause of accidental needle-stick injuries

explanation: Two-handed recapping frequently leads to missed caps and direct punctures into the nurse's hand. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h5)

question: At what maximum level should a puncture-resistant safety box be filled before final closure and disposal?

options.A: Completely full to the very brim

explanation: Filling safety boxes beyond three-quarters increases the risk of protruding sharps piercing the container and injuring staff. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h5)

question: Which waste bin category is appropriate for disposing of blood-soaked cotton swabs and soiled dressings?

options.A: Green bin for organic food leftovers
options.B: Cardboard box for clean paper waste
options.C: Black bin for general municipal refuse

explanation: Infectious waste contaminated with body fluids belongs in yellow biohazard containers for safe incineration or autoclaving. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h6)

question: Why is a designated contact time required when applying a chlorine solution to a blood spill?

options.A: To allow the chemical enough time to destroy pathogens effectively
options.B: To prevent the slippery floor solution from causing patient falls
options.C: To give the liquid time to evaporate completely from the floor
options.D: To neutralize the harsh chemical odor before wiping it away

explanation: Disinfectants require specific contact times to deactivate viruses, bacteria, and other pathogens present in organic spills. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h6)

question: What is the recommended timeframe within which HIV Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) should be initiated for maximum effectiveness?
explanation: PEP must be started as soon as possible, ideally within hours and no later than 72 hours after exposure to prevent viral replication. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h7)

question: What immediate action should a nurse take after experiencing a deep needle-stick injury on the ward?

options.A: Wait until the end of the work shift before filing a report
options.B: Squeeze the puncture site firmly to force out contaminated blood
options.C: Apply undiluted bleach directly into the open wound opening
options.D: Wash the wound immediately with soap and running water

explanation: Washing with soap and water removes surface contaminants without causing further tissue trauma that squeezing would induce. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h7)

question: Why is it important for community health nurses to involve traditional birth attendants in infection control training?

options.A: To enforce strict hospital visitation rules in remote village communities
options.B: To promote safe delivery practices and reduce neonatal infections in rural areas
options.C: To supply commercial pharmaceutical drugs directly to local herbalists
options.D: To replace formal hospital maternity wards with home delivery services entirely

explanation: Engaging traditional birth attendants improves hygiene and prevents transmission of tetanus and other infections during home deliveries. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h8)

question: Which community health activity directly helps protect infants from vaccine-preventable viral infections?

options.A: Distributing bleach solutions to households for kitchen sanitation
options.B: Monitoring vaccine cold chain integrity during immunization drives
options.C: Inspecting local market stalls for expired food and canned goods
options.D: Clearing overgrown bushes and stagnant water around village squares

explanation: Maintaining the cold chain ensures vaccines like Hepatitis B remain potent and effective when administered to infants. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h8)
